none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Unconstrained monotone root finding: a continuous operator F:E→E satisfies ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥0 and has a zero xstar with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R. E is a real inner product space; completeness and finite dimension are not assumed. No objective or gradient representation is required.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact operator evaluation: every query x returns F(x), independently of history and seed. No gradient structure is assumed. The extracted budget counts operator evaluations.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Whenever ‖F(x+θ(y−x))‖≤M for every θ∈[0,1], ‖F(x)−F(y)‖≤(L0+L1 M)‖x−y‖. Parameters satisfy L0>0 and L1≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E,L0,L1,R,x0 are public, with R≥0 and a zero within distance R of x0. The tolerance ε>0 belongs only to Params: algorithm construction does not receive ε, although the execution budget depends on it.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The residual bound holds almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed law, after execution with the supplied fixed oracle budget.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy the unsquared operator residual bound ‖F(output)‖≤ε. There is no prescribed averaging or iterate-selection requirement.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Monotone root finding is classical, but the operator-norm-dependent segment Lipschitz condition is an unusual generalization of global Lipschitz continuity.
